purpose: Make every page communicate one clear, static, colorable story beat instead of a generic character portrait.
principles: One page communicates one primary beat.
Colorability wins every conflict with story complexity.
Express the beat with one clear verb, simple body language, and one environmental interaction.
Prefer stable actions such as stalking, guarding, feeding, hiding, dragging, inspecting, climbing with contact, tending, watching, threatening, or using one object.
Avoid neutral portrait poses where the monster merely stands and holds props.
Avoid simultaneous unrelated actions, extra characters, or multiple props added only to explain the story.
The environment must participate in the beat rather than acting as wallpaper.
Story clarity must not require falling, jumping, chaotic motion, micro-detail, or dense background clutter.
Presence is not enough: required objects must connect, support, cross, point toward, emerge from, or interact with each other exactly as the story beat requires.
automatic_failures: monster reads as posing for a portrait instead of doing the stated moment
story depends only on a held prop with no readable body language
environment does not participate in the moment
multiple competing story beats are present
moment requires unstable jump/fall action to be understood
stated moment is not visually distinguishable at thumbnail size
story adds enough props, figures, or detail to reduce coloring space
story complexity makes the monster silhouette or anatomy harder to color
more than one primary action must be decoded to understand the page
all required objects are present but their spatial/physical relationship makes the story incorrect or ambiguous
review_questions: What single verb describes what the monster is doing?
Can that action be identified without reading the caption?
Does at least one environment feature participate?
Does the pose remain stable and easy to color?
Would removing the prop destroy the entire story read? If yes, strengthen body/environment interaction.
priority_rule: Story makes the page memorable, but colorability wins every conflict. Simplify the beat before adding clutter, extra figures, unstable poses, tiny props, or dense environment detail.

story_budget.secondary_figures: none unless essential; if present, small and simple
story_budget.rule: Express the beat with one clear verb, simple body language, and one environment interaction. Do not build a miniature narrative scene full of objects.

relationship_engine.purpose: Required objects must have correct physical and narrative relationships, not merely appear somewhere in the frame.
relationship_engine.rule: Resolve only relationship rules triggered by the page recipe and append them after the core story beat.
examples: tripwire crosses travel lane and visibly explains pit trigger
wall torch visibly attaches to masonry
offering object aims toward shrine focal point
hanging creature visibly attaches to overhead support
emerging creature visibly intersects and remains supported by the opening
carried object visibly contacts the limb or body carrying it
relationship_engine.review_rule: A page fails story/environment interaction if all required objects are present but their physical relationship is wrong or ambiguous.
